title: LIO-DPC: Accurate and Fast LiDAR-Inertial Odometry with Dynamic Pose Chain
problem: LiDAR-inertial odometry must balance speed and accuracy: filter-based methods are fast but suffer from cumulative errors; graph-based methods reduce errors but are computationally expensive, making real-time operation challenging.
motivation: Robotics, autonomous driving, and drone applications require precise, low-latency motion estimation; current methods force a speed-accuracy tradeoff unsuitable for real-time deployment.
method: The system starts with a fast filter that quickly estimates poses at each moment, then selectively refines them using local graph optimization—checking whether nearby poses fit together correctly. To keep computation manageable, it uses loop sparsification: it identifies representative loops (when the device returns to a location it's seen before) but only checks the ones closest together in time and space, skipping redundant constraints. This selective checking captures the accuracy benefits of graph-based optimization without the computational cost of handling every constraint.
key_novelty: Instead of optimizing the entire path at once like traditional graph-based methods, this system locally refines groups of nearby poses and selectively checks loop closures, combining the speed of filters with the accuracy of graphs.
contributions: Achieves real-time performance with graph-based accuracy
Loop sparsification strategy for computational efficiency
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; specific accuracy metrics and computational overhead comparisons not provided.
primary_theme: Hybrid filter-graph LiDAR odometry for real-time accuracy
